meta.scope: Commonly-used Lumerical script API subset — NOT exhaustive. If a function is not listed here, do NOT assume its signature; call get_lumapi_ref(list_only=true) or check Lumerical documentation.
meta.note: Each entry's verified_against should be updated to the Lumerical version (e.g. '241') after live verification. Mark 'pending' until then.

getresult.returns: dataset object — fields accessed with .f, .lambda, .Ex, .Ey, .Ez, .Hx, .Hy, .Hz, .x, .y, .z, .T, .R, .P, .power depending on monitor type

valid_args.name: monitor name (e.g. 'DFT', 'index') or 'FDTD' for global results
valid_args.property: dataset name, e.g. 'E', 'H', 'T', 'P', 'index' — must match monitor output flags

common_pitfalls: getresult returns a dataset object, not a scalar — use .field access (via getv) to get arrays
Second arg specifies which dataset within the monitor's results; with one arg it returns a list of available datasets

getdata.returns: array of field values (not a dataset object — direct array)
common_pitfalls: getdata returns a raw array, not a dataset — preferred when you want just one field
getresult + getv(dataset.field) is equivalent but returns the whole dataset

getnamed.returns: property value (type depends on property: float, string, array)
common_pitfalls: Property names have spaces (e.g. 'x span', 'wavelength start') — use exact casing
getnamed only works for scalar/string properties; for datasets use getresult
Confirmed working for all 35+ properties in get_scene_info
getnamed.verified_against: proven — used extensively in get_scene_info and get_parameters

valid_args.value: new value — number, string, or array

common_pitfalls: Does NOT work for script properties — use set() with 'setup script'/'analysis script' instead
Property names are case-sensitive and may contain spaces

valid_args.value: new value (string for scripts, number for properties)

common_pitfalls: set() operates on the currently selected object (select() first)
For script content, always use the set_script tool instead of execute('set("setup script",...)')
For non-script properties, use setnamed() which does NOT require select()

addfdtd.returns: none (creates FDTD solver region in new project)
common_pitfalls: Only needed for new blank projects (new tool calls this automatically)
Configure FDTD region via setnamed('FDTD', prop, val) after creation

addrect.returns: none (creates a rectangle structure object, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-generates a name like 'rectangle_1' — capture it via select() + getnamed('name') after creation
Configure via setnamed or set_parameter tool after creation

addcircle.returns: none (creates a circle/cylinder structure object, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Same pattern as addrect — auto-named, configure after creation

addtfsf.returns: none (creates a TFSF plane wave source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Creates a total-field/scattered-field source — auto-named like 'TFSF_1'
Configure direction, wavelength range, injection axis via setnamed after creation

addgaussian.returns: none (creates a Gaussian beam source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'gaussian_1'
For dipole sources use adddipole(), for plane waves use addplane()

addplane.returns: none (creates a plane wave source, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'plane_1'
May not exist in all Lumerical versions — use addtfsf if addplane is unavailable
Auto-named like 'dipole_1'
Set dipole type (Electric/Magnetic) and polarization angle after creation via setnamed
Auto-named like 'power_1'
Set monitor type (2D/3D/1D), output flags via setnamed after creation

addmesh.returns: none (creates a mesh override region, auto-named)
common_pitfalls: Auto-named like 'mesh_1'
Set dx/dy/dz via setnamed for mesh size override
Returns a generated name like 'material_1' — you MUST capture this return value
Built-in database materials (e.g. 'Au (Gold) - Johnson and Christy') need no addmaterial — just assign the name string via setnamed
After addmaterial, configure properties via setmaterial()
Property names vary by material model type — call getmaterial('name') without property to list available properties
nk data expects [wavelengths_array, n_array, k_array] in meters

getmaterial.returns: with property: property value; without property: list of available property names
common_pitfalls: Call getmaterial(name) WITHOUT property first to discover all settable property names

addvar.returns: none (adds a variable to the Model Variables table)

valid_args.name: variable name (shown in GUI Variables tab)

common_pitfalls: Model variables declared via addvar appear in the Variables tab, NOT as getnamed("::model", name) properties
Signature needs live verification against installed Lumerical version

setvar.returns: none (sets a model variable's value in a scope)
common_pitfalls: Scope-aware — setvar('::model', 'LD', val) vs setvar('::model::group', 'param', val)
Signature needs live verification; getnamed may be equivalent for model-level vars
Scope-aware — may differ from getnamed("::model", name) for variables declared via addvar
Signature needs live verification

adduserprop.signature: adduserprop("name", value)  — called from within an object's setup script
adduserprop.returns: none (adds a user-defined property to an analysis/structure group)
common_pitfalls: adduserprop is called in setup scripts (not directly via execute)
Properties created via adduserprop are read via getnamed(obj, "name")
Currently discovered by regex-scanning setup script text in get_parameters

select.returns: none (selects an object, making it the target for subsequent operations)

valid_args.object_name: full path or relative name of an object

common_pitfalls: Many Lumerical functions (set, get, delete) operate on the CURRENTLY SELECTED object — call select() first
selectall() selects all objects in the current scope
groupscope('::model') resets to root scope before select()
delete() takes NO arguments — first call select('name') then delete()
The execute tool handles delete("name") automatically by wrapping select+delete
In Lumerical script LSF: delete; — no parentheses

valid_args.sweep_name: name of the parameter sweep (as defined in the Sweep editor)

common_pitfalls: Throws an error if the sweep has not been run yet — use get_sweep_info first
For individual monitor results within a sweep, access via getresult inside the sweep's analysis script

farfield.returns: none (performs far-field projection on selected monitor in analysis mode)
common_pitfalls: Must be called in analysis mode (switchtolayout first to go back, then run?)
farfieldfilter(α) sets the numerical aperture filter (α∈[0,1]) — α=0.8 is valid but filters at NA=0.8
Results accessed via farfield3d() / farfieldpolar() after farfield() call
Should be called after farfield() projection has been computed
Returns angular distribution data

farfieldpolar.returns: polar far-field data array (angle, amplitude, phase)
common_pitfalls: farfieldpolar3d exists — 3D polar data
farfieldpolar2d exists — 2D polar cross-section
Returns total transmission (T) through the monitor plane
For polarization-resolved transmission use getresult + field component

dipolepower.returns: total power emitted by a dipole source
common_pitfalls: Returns the total radiated power — useful for normalizing Purcell factor calculations
Must be called in analysis mode with the dipole as an active source

haveresult.returns: 1 (true) or 0 (false) — whether the named result exists
common_pitfalls: Use this BEFORE getresult to avoid errors when no results exist yet
Only available in analysis mode (after run)
Saves to Lumerical's working directory unless absolute path is given
For result datasets: matlabsave('out.mat', _br_d) after _br_d = getresult(...)

switchtolayout.returns: none (switches FDTD solver to layout mode)
common_pitfalls: After running a simulation, you're in analysis mode — switchtolayout() returns to layout mode for editing
Saving and reopening a .fsp also returns to layout mode
